youtube_description:
In the summer of 1616, the most trusted adviser in Japan lay dying in a plain mansion, owning less land than men who had never advised anyone. Decades earlier, he had taken up arms against his own lord, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and been forgiven. Ieyasu, they say, called him friend. What was Honda Masanobu really after? Follow time-travelling reporter Tokio Kamiya as he files a dispatch from Edo, 1616.

📰 Your reporter: Tokio Kamiya, a former Tokyo foreign correspondent. His grandfather's brass pocket watch carries him to one day of Japan's past at a time. He can watch and he can speak, but he can never change what happens. Every episode is his dispatch from the scene.

He is born in Mikawa to a family of modest retainers, and a tradition says he begins as a falconer in the household of the young Ieyasu. What he has is a mind. Many of his contemporaries call him cunning, and they do not always mean it kindly.

He is said to have travelled to Kaga, and to have served the warlord Matsunaga Hisahide in the Kinai. I cannot follow every step. What I can say is that he spends long years as a man with no lord, watching other masters rise and fall. I think that is where he learns what makes power last.
